w: Monte Antelao, highest peak of the eastern Dolomites, is dubbed the King of the Dolomites (Marmolada, taller overall, is the Queen). A steep rock pyramid rather than part of a massif, it was first summited in 1850 by hunter Matteo Ossi, who guided Paul Grohmann up in 1863. On clear days it is visible from Trieste.
s: The King of the Dolomites, first climbed in 1850
_facts: Highest peak of the eastern Dolomites, called the King of the Dolomites
First summited 1850 by hunter Matteo Ossi; guided Paul Grohmann up in 1863
Visible from Trieste on the Adriatic in good weather

w: Falzarego Pass, at 2,105m, links Agordo to Cortina d'Ampezzo and was fought over ferociously in WWI. A gondola climbs to Lagazuoi (2,762m), scene of underground mine warfare between Italian and Austro-Hungarian troops; the tunnel Italian sappers dug beneath enemy lines still stands, open to the public.
s: WWI mine-warfare tunnels beneath a Dolomite pass
_facts: 2,105m pass linking Agordo and Cortina d'Ampezzo
Gondola rises to Lagazuoi (2,762m), site of WWI mine warfare
Italian-built tunnel under Austro-Hungarian lines is open to the public

w: Established 1990 within Cortina d'Ampezzo, this park protects famous Dolomite groups - the Tofane, Monte Cristallo, Croda Rossa, Lagazuoi, Pomagagnon. With the adjoining Fanes-Sennes-Prags park across the province line, it forms 37,000 protected hectares, home to about 1,500 chamois and reintroduced ibex.
s: 37,000 protected hectares covering the Tofane and Lagazuoi
_facts: Established 1990, entirely within Cortina d'Ampezzo comune
Encompasses the Tofane, Monte Cristallo, Croda Rossa, Lagazuoi, Pomagagnon
With adjacent Fanes-Sennes-Prags park forms 37,000 protected hectares
About 1,500 chamois; Alpine ibex reintroduced in early 2000s

w: Lago di Sorapiss sits at 1,925m in the Dolomites, 12km from Cortina, its turquoise color coming from glacial rock flour in the water. No road reaches it: only foot or helicopter, via a 10.5km trail taking 1.5 hours from Passo Tre Croci. The Alta Via 3 and 4 both pass around its shore.
s: A turquoise glacial lake reachable only on foot
_facts: 1,925m altitude, c. 12km from Cortina d'Ampezzo
Turquoise color from glacial dust in the water
Reached only on foot or by helicopter; 10.5km trail from Passo Tre Croci
Alta Via 3 and Alta Via 4 both loop around the lake

w: Named for Romano and Armando Apollonio, this rink was built as a subsidiary to the Olympic Ice Stadium, hosting overflow ice hockey at the 1956 Winter Olympics. Enlarged from 47 by 85m to 62.5 by 85m for two simultaneous matches, seating doubled from 1,000 to 2,000 for the Games. Today it hosts tennis.
s: 1956 Olympic ice hockey rink, now a tennis court
_facts: Built as subsidiary rink to Olympic Ice Stadium for 1956 Winter Olympics
Enlarged from 47x85m to 62.5x85m to run two games at once
Seating expanded from 1,000 to 2,000 for the Games; now used for tennis

w: Becco di Mezzodi takes its name - Midday Peak - from the way the sun sits directly above its summit at noon, seen from Cortina below. Part of the Croda da Lago chain at 2,603m, it is a proper climb rather than a walk: routes start from the Rifugio Croda da Lago on the road to Giau Pass and call for gear and slings.
s: Midday Peak: the sun sits over it at noon from Cortina
_facts: 2,603m, Croda da Lago chain, central Dolomites
Name means Midday Peak - sun appears above it at noon from Cortina
Climbed from Rifugio Croda da Lago; requires gear and slings

n: Cappella della Beata Vergine di Lourdes
w: Also known as the Chiesetta di Grava, this chapel in Cortina's Grava di Sotto quarter was built in 1907 with interior work by Val Gardena artist Corrado Pitscheider. Large windows light a nave holding a Lourdes grotto replica and statues of the Virgin, Bernadette, Lucia and Michael; feast day 11 February.
s: A 1907 chapel with its own Lourdes grotto replica
_facts: Built 1907, also known as Chiesetta di Grava
Interior work by artist Corrado Pitscheider of Val Gardena
Contains a Lourdes grotto replica and statues of Virgin, Bernadette, Lucia, Michael
Feast day 11 February

w: Castello di Botestagno - also called Podestagno, or Peutelstein in German - is a ruined medieval fort in the Veneto's Dolomitic Alps, perched on a rock in the Boite River valley a little north of Cortina d'Ampezzo, near the hamlet of Pra del Castel.
s: A ruined medieval fort above the Boite River
_facts: Also known as Podestagno or Peutelstein
Ruined medieval fort on a rock in the Boite River valley
North of Cortina d'Ampezzo, near Pra del Castel

w: Perched at 1,780m above Cortina, this observatory's two domes hold a 20-inch Newtonian and an 11-inch Schmidt-Cassegrain telescope, run remotely via a system called Sky on the Web. Its amateurs hunt comets and galaxies via the CROSS supernova program, credited with 30 supernovae and one minor planet, 50240 Cortina.
s: A remote-controlled observatory that found 30 supernovae
_facts: 1,780m on Col Drusciè; 20-inch Newtonian and 11-inch Schmidt-Cassegrain telescopes
Remote-control system Sky on the Web for telescope operation
CROSS program has found 30 supernovae and one minor planet (50240 Cortina)
